content: Peropsin is a protein encoded by the RRH gene in humans. It is classified as an opsin, which is a type of G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR). Opsins are light-sensitive proteins, and peropsin shares structural and functional similarities with visual pigments. The RRH gene, like the genes encoding neuropsin and RGR-opsin, is organized into seven exons. Peropsins are part of the Go/RGR opsin subgroup, which is also referred to as RGR/Go or Group 4 opsins. This subgroup is one of the four primary groups of type-II opsins, commonly known as metazoan or animal opsins. The Go/RGR opsins are further divided into four distinct groups: Go-opsins, RGR-opsins, peropsins, and neuropsins. Animal opsins, as a whole, are categorized into four major classes: C-opsins (ciliary opsins), R-opsins (rhabdomeric opsins), Cnidops (opsins found in cnidarians), and Go/RGR-opsins. Among these, three subgroups—C-opsins, R-opsins, and Go/RGR-opsins—are found exclusively in bilaterian animals. However, the bilaterian opsin clades form a paraphyletic group when the Cnidops are excluded.
